identityReview: Joshua Wong Chi-fung / 黃之鋒, Hong Kong activist born 13 October 1996; birth date supported by the RFK Human Rights educational biography and birth year by his accessible NLR interview. Scholarism and Demosisto are distinct organisations; Demosisto dissolved on 30 June 2020, and Nathan Law was its founding chair. Wong is not given a current office in a dissolved organisation. Separate the Civic Square unlawful-assembly case, Mong Kok contempt case, 2024 primary-election subversion sentence and 2025–2026 collusion case. Recent courtroom reporting confirms he remained imprisoned in November 2026.
lifeStatusEvidence: Reuters’s 5 November 2026 report describes Wong physically present at the sentencing hearing, including his gestures to the public gallery. RTHK and the government corroborate the delivered sentence. This is actual recent activity, not solely an old portrait, a database living-person label or a future hearing notice. No photographs or courtroom footage were inspected.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read the RFK biography page, accessible NLR interview opening, government 2012 policy statement, Anadolu 2016 launch report, complete short 2018 DOJ case summary, relevant HRW 2018 account, Reuters 2020 dissolution report, selected D19 sections and sentence table of the 2024 judicial PDF and official case-summary passages, Reuters 2025 charge report, RTHK 2026 plea and sentence accounts, government November sentencing release, Reuters November courtroom/profile reporting and HRW criticism. Read Commons descriptions/licensing/history without image pixels.
corrections: Read the Joshua Wong student-biography page in the RFK Human Rights classroom PDF. It explicitly gives birth in Hong Kong on 13 October 1996. This is a secondary educational biography, not a birth register. Its broader discussion of 2047 and its compressed accounts of arrests, imprisonment and appeals are not used as authoritative legal chronology. No unverified university degree, family detail, health history or present organisational office is imported.

Read the accessible opening of Wong’s March–April 2015 New Left Review interview. His first-person account describes a 1996 Hong Kong birth and organising with friends in May 2011 around opposition to the proposed Moral and National Education curriculum. The exact founding month is attributed to this retrospective self-report; the whole interview beyond the accessible extract was not reviewed. His broad claims about the unprecedented nature of student participation are not independently adopted.

Read the Hong Kong government’s 8 September 2012 policy announcement. It removed the deadline after the three-year initiation period and left schools and school-sponsoring bodies to decide whether, how and when to introduce the subject, with curriculum guidance subject to review. This was not a permanent ban on national education or a claim that all civic education ceased. The government attributed its decision to multiple stakeholders; the public biography does not credit Wong alone with the policy change.

Read Anadolu’s 10 April 2016 launch report, updated 18 April. It distinguishes Nathan Law as party chair and Wong, formerly of Scholarism, as the new organisation’s secretary, and reports proposed electoral and international-advocacy activity. Public wording uses the well-supported co-founder role rather than extending an old title to 2026. The article mistakenly places the long Occupy street protests in late 2015; this is not adopted, as the 2014 chronology is corroborated by court summaries and other reporting. Proposed referendum options, forecasts and the article’s categorical treatment of 2047 are not imported as settled constitutional outcomes.

Read the complete short Department of Justice summary of FACC 8–10/2017, [2018] HKCFA 4. It identifies the 26 September 2014 forecourt incident, trial convictions and original 80-hour community-service order for Wong, the 17 August 2017 sentence review, and the 6 February 2018 successful appeals against sentence. Its June 2018 publication is not the judgment date. The CFA accepted that stricter guidance could apply to future cases while finding no proper basis to alter the earlier magistrate’s reasonable sentence. This is not an acquittal or a holding that all protest-related conduct is lawful. It is a departmental judgment summary, not the full original judgment.

Read Human Rights Watch’s contemporaneous 6 February 2018 account, including the explicit reinstatement of Wong’s completed 80-hour community-service order and the separate Mong Kok contempt case. It corroborates the outcome of the sentencing appeal, while its normative criticism remains attributed. The other activists’ suspended sentence and service hours are not assigned to Wong. The 2018 description of bail or potential further imprisonment is not carried forward as his current legal status.

Read Reuters’s contemporaneous 30 June 2020 report via Daily Maverick. It records passage of the national security law and Demosisto’s announcement of dissolution that day while details and commencement were still expected later. Therefore the event is not described as occurring only after the law had already taken effect. The national legislature’s enactment, an organisation’s dissolution and subsequent individual prosecutions are separate events. The article does not establish the exact hour or every member’s resignation sequence.

Read selected D19 passages within paragraphs 154–161 and the final sentence table in the court’s 2024 reasons for sentence, hosted by Columbia Global Freedom of Expression. They identify Wong Chi-fung, his accepted active-participant classification, a seven-year starting point, one-third reduction for guilty plea and final four years eight months (56 months). Do not mistake D29, another defendant also sentenced to 56 months, for Wong. His 2024 mitigation did not raise mistake of law, unlike arguments made in the later 2026 case. No complete read of every defendant’s evidence or later appeal record is claimed. Direct judiciary-frame access was unavailable; the mirrored judicial PDF was readable.

Read the official national-security case summary header and background and the heading identifying D19. It confirms HCCC 69/2022, [2024] HKCFI 3298, 19 November 2024 sentencing, a conspiracy-to-commit-subversion count and the alleged plan involving a legislative majority, indiscriminate budget refusal and government paralysis. The case concerned more than the bare fact of voting in a primary. Forty-seven defendants were charged, but 45 were sentenced after guilty pleas or trial convictions; do not say all 47 were convicted on one day. The public profile does not claim Wong’s guilty plea occurred on the May 2024 trial-verdict date for other defendants.

Read Reuters’s 6 June 2025 court report via StreetInsider. It describes a new conspiracy-to-collude charge while Wong was already serving the primary-case sentence; the charge sheet’s period is 1 July–23 November 2020. His court response that he understood the charge is not a guilty plea. A separate police suspicion concerning property is not automatically an additional charge, conviction or part of the later sentence. The historical expected January 2027 release is superseded by the November 2026 sentence; the article’s file photo from March 2021 is not a new June 2025 photograph.

Read RTHK’s 2 September 2026 report of Wong’s guilty plea and mitigation, with sentencing adjourned at that stage. Prosecution references to older international-lobbying arrangements are distinct from the charged post-commencement period. The defence’s discussion of the pre-existing sentence and January 2027 expected completion does not fix his release after the later case. Do not leave this profile at the outdated awaiting-sentence stage.

Read the Hong Kong government’s 5 November 2026 English announcement and the central passages of its Chinese counterpart. They state that Wong pleaded guilty on 2 September and was sentenced that day to ten years for conspiracy to commit collusion under Article 29. The release reports the court’s grave-offence assessment but also includes the chief executive’s and government spokesperson’s political condemnation. Those statements are attributed government positions, not independent biographical character judgments. The full 2026 reasons for sentence were not inspected; official reporting is corroborated by RTHK and Reuters. No final outcome of a future appeal or completed asset confiscation is asserted.

Read RTHK’s 5 November 2026 sentencing report, especially the judge’s starting point, reduction and two months plus two days concurrent with the existing subversion sentence. This is more precise than rounding concurrency to two months and rules out simply adding ten years to the full earlier term. The ten-year sentence is not described as life imprisonment. No independent prison-calculation record, remission decision or definitive release date was obtained.

Read Reuters’s 5 November 2026 courtroom report via Investing.com. It describes Wong’s actual presence and gestures in court, the delivered ten-year sentence, September plea, charged July–November 2020 conduct, mitigation remarks and government responses. The hosting site’s 4 November US-time publication label does not move the Hong Kong sentencing to 4 November. His denial of advocating independence or receiving foreign funding, and the government’s contrary political characterisations, remain attributed; the public profile does not turn either into a blanket factual description. The appearance supplies recent life-status evidence without claiming to have viewed photos or video.

Read Human Rights Watch’s 5 November 2026 criticism and call for unconditional release. The account is a human-rights assessment, not a court order vacating convictions. Its rounded two-month overlap is less precise than RTHK’s two months and two days, and its projected late-2036 release is not copied as certain. Its compressed January 2021 charged chronology is not used to establish an exact arrest/charging date in the primary case. Distinguish NGO assessments of freedom of expression from government views of national security and from adjudicated outcomes.

Read relevant passages of Reuters’s 5 November 2026 profile via Investing.com. It corroborates early Scholarism activism, the Umbrella Movement and sustained international visibility. Do not describe Wong as the sole organiser of a broad movement, confuse a magazine cover or Nobel nomination with winning an award, or adopt the profile’s loose toddler-age phrasing as a birth record. Claims that protests forced a policy change are tempered by the separately reviewed government policy text and acknowledgement of multiple participants.

additionalConsulted.access: Read DOJ’s contemporaneous statement, including original community-service orders, sentence-review procedure and withdrawal of conviction appeals in 2017. Its position on civil disobedience is attributed to the authority; use the fuller short decision summary and independent account for sentence-appeal outcome.
Direct judiciary frame was inaccessible via the research tool. Read selected relevant passages in the judicial PDF hosted by Columbia, not every page.
Read ACCORD catalogue metadata identifying BBC’s 10 April 2016 Demosisto launch report. This is a catalogue record, not the article body.
Opening exposed navigation rather than the substantive article in the returned viewport; no full-body review claimed. The readable Anadolu article supplies launch details.
Attempted related article path failed. No assertions rely on its unseen body.

Search index supplied a dated author biography describing Demosisto office in the present tense; opening exposed a video/navigation shell. Not used to establish a 2026 current office, completed degree or exact book-publication history.
Read Chinese sentence announcement to check the formal offence name, 2 September plea and 5 November ten-year sentence; political commentary remains attributed.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human/native-language review. No birth certificate, full university record, complete 2018 or 2026 original judgment, complete 2024 trial and appellate record, prison release calculation or portrait pixels were inspected. The timeline is selective, not an exhaustive criminal-case ledger. Refresh appeals and custody status before release. Avoid collapsing charge, plea, conviction, sentencing and appeal; no presumed future release date, retrospective acquittal, blanket political label or unverified sole-causation claim.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed against Chinese and English. Preserve the 1996 birthday; May 2011 attributed founding account; 2012 removal of a deadline versus abolition of all national education; multi-actor Umbrella Movement; Nathan Law’s party chair role and Demosisto dissolution; 2018 sentence reversal versus acquittal and separate contempt case; 56 months equals four years eight months in the 2024 primary case; June 2025 charge versus September 2026 plea and November sentence; two months and two days concurrency versus simple addition of terms; government positions and NGO criticism as attributed assessments. Arabic subversion wording refers to undermining state power, not generic physical sabotage.
